# 11 — Space Travel & Planet Transitions

Travel works like **No Man's Sky**: one continuous universe with no loading screens. Take off from the surface, climb out of the atmosphere, pulse across the system, drop out at a planet, burn through its atmosphere and land, then step out and walk. Every transition is a short, spectacular sequence that also hides streaming. Unlike NMS, your ship is something you built, so its thrust, mass and gyroscopes shape how it flies.

## Principles

1. **Seamless.** Surface ↔ orbit ↔ system ↔ system without a loading screen. Loads hide inside the launch, entry, pulse and jump sequences.
2. **Assisted by default.** Arcade-friendly flight with auto-levelling, terrain clearance, one-button launch and landing, and no orbital mechanics to master.
3. **Your build still matters.** Thrust sets acceleration and top speed (within the caps below), gyroscopes set turn rate, mass sets inertia, and a ship can't launch without enough thrust (auto-launch needs thrust-to-weight ≥ 1.2 in local gravity).
4. **Spectacle at every threshold.** Atmosphere entry, cloud punch-through, the sky fading to stars, pulse streaks, the jump tunnel.
5. **Newtonian mode for purists.** A settings toggle switches to full Space Engineers-style physics (inertial dampeners, real gravity falloff, no speed caps).

## Flight speeds (assisted mode)

| Regime | Cruise | Boost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Atmospheric flight | 30–250 m/s | 400 m/s | Holds ≥ 15 m terrain clearance unless landing |
| Airless approach (below the approach altitude) | up to 400 m/s | — | Retro-burn VFX; lets voxel streaming keep up |
| Space (impulse) | up to 1,200 m/s | 2,000 m/s | Scaled by the ship's thrust-to-mass |
| Pulse drive | spools 3 s, reaches 30 km/s in 15 s | — | Blocked below 0.5 R altitude; drops out automatically |
| Jump (system to system) | 10 s charge + 8–12 s tunnel | — | Arrives 10–20 km from the destination system's station or beacon; 5 min cooldown |

## The journey, step by step

```
LANDED ─[hold Launch]→ LIFT-OFF (30 m in 3 s) → ATMOSPHERIC FLIGHT (250 m/s, terrain clearance)
   → CLIMB → ATMOSPHERE EXIT (sky fades to black, stars pop in, 5 s) → SPACE (1,200 m/s)
   → PULSE (spool 3 s, up to 30 km/s; encounters may interrupt) → AUTO DROPOUT at the target's pulse altitude
   → APPROACH → ATMOSPHERE ENTRY (heat streaks, shake, speed capped over 4 s; 8 s sequence) → CLOUD PUNCH-THROUGH
   → ATMOSPHERIC FLIGHT → LANDING PROMPT below 150 m over ground ≤ 20° or a pad → AUTO-LAND (6 s) → STEP OUT
```

| Step | What the player sees | What the engine does meanwhile |
|---|---|---|
| **Launch** | Thrusters roar, dust kicks up, the ship lifts and levels | Physics grid switches from landed (static) to flying; checks thrust-to-weight |
| **Atmosphere exit** | Sky darkens, stars appear, wind noise drops away | Unloads high-detail voxel rings behind the ship; loads the system view |
| **Pulse** | Streaks, the target planet swelling ahead, ETA on the HUD | Pre-streams the target planet's coarse clipmap and nearby points of interest |
| **Dropout** | A thump; the planet fills the canopy | Floating-origin rebase; encounter roll resolved |
| **Atmosphere entry** | Heat plasma, shaking canopy, glow, then clouds | Streams full-resolution voxels around the predicted landing area within the entry sequence |
| **Landing** | Gear down, the ship settles on a pad or flat ground | Ship grid becomes static; no-build and landing-zone volumes checked |
| **Jump** | The galaxy-map target locks, the ship charges, a glyph-lit tunnel | Unloads the old system, loads the new one (masked by the tunnel) |

## Per-planet thresholds

| Planet | Diameter | Pulse dropout | Atmosphere entry / approach | Cloud deck | Streaming starts | Capital parking | Dropout → landed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Earth (starter planet) | 120 km | 30.0 km | 9,000 m | 3,600 m | 360.0 km from centre | 24.0 km | 74 s |
| The Moon | 40 km | 10.0 km | 3,000 m (airless cap) | — | 120.0 km from centre | 8,000 m | 22 s |
| Veyra-4 | 100 km | 25.0 km | 7,500 m | 3,000 m | 300.0 km from centre | 20.0 km | 63 s |
| Hollowmere | 80 km | 20.0 km | 6,000 m | 2,400 m | 240.0 km from centre | 16.0 km | 52 s |
| Drift Planet (procedural) | 120 km | 30.0 km | 9,000 m | 3,600 m | 360.0 km from centre | 24.0 km | 74 s |

Thresholds are fractions of each planet's radius: pulse dropout at 0.5 R altitude, atmosphere top at 0.15 R, clouds at 40% of the atmosphere, streaming from 6 R.

## Ships by size

| Ship | Lands on planets? | Travel | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small grid (landers, fighters, shuttles) | Yes: auto-land on flat ground or pads | Atmosphere, space, pulse | Needs landing gear or legs for auto-land |
| Medium (large-grid utility ships) | Yes, on pads ≥ 30 m or flat ground ≥ 40 m | All, including pulse | Needs a Guidance Computer for auto-land |
| Capital ships (the Second Chance and larger) | **No**: park in orbit, like NMS freighters | Pulse and jump | Summon to the current system through the Jump Core; shuttle down in a small craft, or use a Beacon Relay |

## Stations & docking

| Bay | Size | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Small hangar bay | 30 × 20 × 15 m | Landers, fighters, small-grid ships |
| Medium hangar bay | 60 × 40 × 25 m | Medium ships; auto-dock inside the approach cone below 100 m/s |
| Capital docking arm | External clamp, 200 m clearance | Large-grid capital ships (they never enter bays) |

Every Drift system has at least one dockable station (a Hauler waystation, a Directorate outpost or a Sower relay). Entering a bay's approach cone below 100 m/s triggers auto-dock.

## Encounters in transit

- Pulse travel rolls for an interruption about 5% of the time per minute: Directorate patrols in their territory, Hauler raiders, spore-swarms near Bloomed systems, derelict distress calls.
- An interruption drops the ship into a combat bubble; the pulse drive re-spools once it's clear or the player escapes the bubble (5 km).
- Story beats never interrupt the player mid-pulse (game bible 08 §8.7).

## Level design rules for travel

1. **Readable from orbit.** Every anchor needs a landmark visible from its planet's pulse-dropout altitude (a glow, beacon or megastructure), and a waypoint label once scanned.
2. **Land close to the action.** A `VOL_LandingZone` (a flat area ≥ 40 m or a pad) within 300 m of every anchor entrance; interiors that forbid ships use `VOL_NoFly`.
3. **Station bays use the metrics above**; scripted approaches (Haven-9 docking in M2.01, the Seedship breach in M4.01) are drawn as `SPL_Approach_*` splines.
4. **No hard ceilings.** The atmosphere top is a soft transition, never a wall; the only no-fly zones are story interiors and the Seedship.
5. **Entry sequences are budgets.** Entry and jump sequences must cover the streaming they hide: designers never place a landing zone where the full-detail voxel radius (2 km) can't stream within the 8 s entry.

## Controls (same as game bible 21 §21.3, Ship flight)

| Action | KB/M | Controller |
|---|---|---|
| Launch (when landed) | Space (hold) | A (hold) |
| Land (at the prompt) | F (hold) | X (hold) |
| Boost | Left Alt (hold) | L3 |
| Pulse drive (in space) | J (hold) | Hold Menu + A |
| Galaxy map | M | View |
| Sower jump | M, select a system, hold J | View, select, hold A |
| Flight assist ↔ Newtonian (per ship) | Z (hold) | B (hold) |
| Summon capital ship | Wrist pad → Fleet | Wrist pad → Fleet |

## Blender spec

- Planet scaffolds (chapter 03) add transition shells: `REF_PulseDropout`, `REF_Atmosphere` (entry), `REF_CloudDeck`, `REF_StreamingStart` and `REF_CapitalParking`, so designers see every threshold at true scale.
- Levels mark travel with `VOL_LandingZone_*`, `VOL_DockingBay_*`, `VOL_NoFly_*` and `SPL_Approach_*`; all are exported to the `.markers.json` sidecar.
